Q: Debugging error and success notices prior to parsing data A:

The format for the hook you are adding, is admin_post_{$action}.

add_action('admin_post_import_file', [$this, 'handle_upload']);

So this means, the action name you chose is import_file.

<input type="hidden" name="action" value="i_import_file">

You used a different value here, i_import_file - so submitting this form will not trigger the action hook you configured via your code. The value here needs to be import_file, matching the suffix you used when adding the action.

Q: Why is Ninja not compiling my RC file correctly? A:

This is not, yet, a complete answer.

The first part of the answer is to install the mingw-w64-x86_64-cmake-cmcldeps or equivalent. This changes the rules.ninja to read something like:

rule RC_COMPILER__test_unscanned_Debug
  depfile = $DEP_FILE
  deps = gcc
  command = C:/msys64/mingw64/bin/cmcldeps.exe RC $in $DEP_FILE $out "Note: including file: " "C:/Program Files/Microsoft Visual Studio/18/Community/VC/Tools/MSVC/14.50.35717/bin/Hostx64/x64/cl.exe" ${LAUNCHER}${CODE_CHECK}C:\PROGRA~2\WI3CF2~1\10\bin\100261~1.0\x64\rc.exe $DEFINES $INCLUDES $FLAGS /fo $out $in
  description = Building RC object $out

I still get the same error, but if I run the reported command manually, escaping all the \, then the command completes without errors but does not actually generate a file. Using / instead of \ does generate the same error.

Upon investigation, cmcldeps wants a path to an object file. Specifying an empty extra field almost works, but then cl.exe complains that it cannot find the *.res file that we are trying to create. Using touch to generate an empty file then works.

CMake bug raised here.

Q: RegEx Find all words that are NOT in line with a starting Single Quote A:

You could use lookahead for that. Just use (?=^[^']) at the beginning, which is positive lookahead assuring that line starts with something different than '.

Full patern:

(?=^[^'])(?:.*\b(CreateObject|Set|Open)\b)

Except for the lookahead, I just added ?:, which means non capturing group and .* to consume any characters until wanted text.

Regex 101

Q: How do I further optimize this prefix sum question? A:

From what ive understood, updates in this scenario are just new test cases derived from the original case by changing Ai and Bi to a and b.
I may not remember the code exact line by line but I do remember the logic of it.
Right, I forgot to include the line that updates are permanent.
So, if initially A and B are:
1 2 3 4
4 3 2 2
and then there is an update with i, a and b being 2 7 and 6 respectively, then the A and B would be:
1 7 3 4
4 6 2 2
and then I have to find the minimum for this as well. To do so, I recalculate the prefix sums from the position i.
If you read the comment, it tells how values of A and B are stored in the array. So, for i = 2, in array A, it would be at index 2 and for array B, it would be at index 1.
And as updates are permanent, same code can be used for multiple updates.

Q: Inner/Outer SELECT filtering A:

The general answer is that the first version would be performant than the second. The reason for this is that in the first version, the WHERE clause can filter off records earlier than the second version. Specifically, in the second version, the outer filter has to deal with a union of all records from the 2 tables. Therefore, there would be more work as SQL Server has to comb through the larger intermediate result to remove non matching records.

However, there is another important point to consider here. Should the two tables happen to have an index on ColA, that index could be used to rapidly remove non matching records from the inner queries on both of the 2 tables. The union operation, then, would add very minimal work to the execution plan of the query (it uses UNION ALL, which basically justs combines the two result sets with no deduplication logic). But in the case of the second query, it filters on ColA after the large union all has happened. This outer filtering cannot use any index on ColA, because it would be filtering on an intermediate result set/table. The first version, on the other hand, is sargable to an index on ColA.

As a rule of thumb, you would be aiming to use the first version.

Q: Conditionally format color to extra tick mark in matplotlib A:

Since you need to mark the ticks that are not presented yet, why not just move the:

index_d = xticks.index(d)        
plt.gca().get_xticklines()[index_d].set_markeredgecolor('red')

inside the if block?

So it would be:

for i, d in enumerate(ds):
    plt.imshow(2Darray, interpolation='none', extent=[left, right, bottom, top], aspect='auto' )

    xticks = list(plt.xticks()[0])     #get x-axis ticks
    if d not in xticks:                     #if d is not in the x-axis ticks 
        plt.xticks(xticks + [d])            #add d to x-axis ticks
        new_xticks = list(plt.xticks()[0])      #get new x-axis ticks
        index_d = new_xticks.index(d)           #find index where d is
        plt.gca().get_xticklabels()[index_d].set_visible(False) #hide the tick label for the d tick just created

        # ---- Move here
        index_d = xticks.index(d)        
        plt.gca().get_xticklines()[index_d].set_markeredgecolor('red')
        # --------------

    xticks = list(plt.xticks()[0])          #get x-axis ticks again since d may have been added

Q: What's the difference between 'git switch' and 'git checkout' <branch>? A:

The answer by M. Justin was really great. However, I just noticed that there is a difference in the behavior between git checkout --orphan and git switch --orphan:

git checkout --orphan new-branch
git status

Output:

On branch new-branch

No commits yet

Changes to be committed:
.....

will checkout to the new-branch and will keep the tracked files.

While using switch will erase all the tracked files with a literally fresh branch:

git switch --orphan new-branch
git status

Output:

Switched to a new branch 'new-branch'

My Git version is 2.34.1.

a reproducal example (even with git 2.48.1):

the initial setup:

mkdir test
cd test/
git init
touch file.txt README.md
git add file.txt README.md
git commit -m 'init'
